programme: LMO2 transcriptionally sits upstream of MECOM (MECOM is a direct LMO2 target), and both are core components of the hematopoietic/lymphoid stem-and-progenitor self-renewal transcriptional circuit that also includes the self-renewal homeobox genes HOXA11 and HOXB4; this is the same module that, when ectopically reactivated, drives T-lineage leukemic/lymphomatous transformation.
role_in_a: Correlative only: LMO2 appears among genes with altered expression in a transgenic AD brain transcriptome and MECOM appears in a blood biomarker panel for AD; neither paper demonstrates a functional role for the module in neurons or glia, so at best this is a proposed peripheral/transcriptomic signature, not an established mechanism.
role_in_b: LMO2 is a well-characterized oncogenic driver of T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, is used diagnostically (IHC) to identify T-lymphoblastic disease, and thymoma is documented to co-occur with LMO2-driven T-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma in the same patients — giving this module a genuine, if indirect (via co-occurring T-ALL rather than the epithelial thymoma itself), place in thymic disease.
shared_axis: If the same stem/progenitor self-renewal transcriptional module (LMO2-MECOM plus HOX self-renewal genes) that is causally reactivated in T-lineage neoplasia adjacent to thymoma were also aberrantly reactivated in AD-vulnerable neurons — consistent with the broader hypothesis that AD neurons re-engage cell-cycle/developmental programs before degenerating — that would explain why the same factor set recurs in both tissues; nothing in the retrieved material demonstrates this directly, it is inferred from the LMO2→MECOM link and the factors' known developmental function.
reasoning: The module is nameable from the factors alone (LMO2 directly regulates MECOM; HOXA11/HOXB4 are canonical HSC self-renewal genes) and LMO2 plus MECOM are each independently placed in one of the two diseases by retrieved papers, so this clears 'weak'. But no retrieved source connects AD and thymoma through this module, HOXA11/HOXB4 have zero disease-specific evidence, and brain-thymus is not an anatomically obvious pairing, so it falls short of 'strong' or 'supported'.
support: PMID 40186694 — LMO2 among genes altered in a transgenic AD brain transcriptome; PMID 39093073 — MECOM among candidate blood biomarkers in AD; PMID 38358204 — LMO2 immunohistochemistry distinguishes T-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma; PMID 40344914 — LMO2 as a pan-cancer immunotherapy marker that inhibits tumor progression; PMID 40224340 — case report of thymoma co-occurring with acute T-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (the disease LMO2 drives); PMID 23414597 — explicitly reports no association of TP73 with AD in mouse models or human cohorts, which is why TP73, despite 80/80 concordance, is not carried into this programme.
how_to_falsify: Profile LMO2, MECOM, HOXA11 and HOXB4 expression by single-nucleus RNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics in AD hippocampus/cortex versus age-matched controls to see whether they are genuinely reactivated in neurons or glia (not just present via blood/immune-cell contamination of bulk tissue); in parallel, run ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN for LMO2 at the MECOM locus in thymic and neuronal tissue. If LMO2/MECOM show no neuronal or glial expression above background, do not co-vary with disease state, or LMO2 does not occupy the MECOM locus outside hematopoietic lineages, the shared-module account is falsified.
caveats: Brain and thymus are not an anatomically or clinically expected pairing, and no clinical or epidemiological literature links AD and thymoma. The concordance is drawn from 80 patient-group comparisons across only 3 independent cohort pairs, so replication is coarse. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed NOTCH1, TAL1, ZEB1, GATA-adjacent and other classic T-cell/thymic master regulators — the factors that would have made a thymic story obvious — so the LMO2/MECOM/HOX module surviving here is a secondary layer, not the tissue's dominant circuit, and should be read as such. The single-view exclusions (POU2F3, ZNF571, DMAP1) confirm this account is not an artifact of one idiosyncratic subgroup. Most of the 12 listed factors (TP73, CDX1, GCM1, NCOA6, TBP, NFKBIB, ZGPAT, PATZ1) have no usable disease-specific evidence and were deliberately left out of the programme rather than forced into it.
